![The product lifecycle: a complete overview | PM-Partners](https://api.dataforseo.com/cdn/i/10081734-2633-0066-0000-b6ea70160b8c:4)
The product life cycle `tracks a product's journey from its initial conception and market launch to its eventual removal from the market`.[[1]](https://fractory.com/product-life-cycle-explained/)

### The Four Core Stages

The [Product Life Cycle Explained](https://www.investopedia.com/terms/p/product-life-cycle.asp) model breaks down a product's commercial life into four primary phases:[[1]](https://www.investopedia.com/terms/p/product-life-cycle.asp)

- **Introduction:** The product is newly launched into the market. Sales are low and growth is slow because demand must still be built. Marketing and advertising costs are at their highest as companies work to create brand awareness and educate consumers.[[1]](https://www.coursera.org/articles/product-lifecycle)[[2]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CUtsYPGydKk)
- **Growth:** The product gains market acceptance and momentum. Sales and revenues increase rapidly, production scales up, and profit margins expand as costs per unit drop. Competitors often enter the market during this phase.[[1]](https://www.salesforce.com/au/blog/product-life-cycle/)[[2]](https://www.fool.com/terms/p/product-life-cycle/)[[3]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CUtsYPGydKk)[[4]](https://www.coursera.org/articles/product-lifecycle)[[5]](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/G5Mq71vDX7U?vl=en-US)
- **Maturity:** Sales velocity slows down and levels off as the market approaches saturation. This is typically the most profitable stage because manufacturing and promotional costs have stabilized or declined. Competition is fierce, requiring strong product differentiation and branding.[[1]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0GsSTBI8Zkk&t=3)[[2]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CUtsYPGydKk)[[3]](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/G5Mq71vDX7U?vl=en-US)[[4]](https://www.salesforce.com/in/blog/product-life-cycle/)
- **Decline:** Sales and profits drop steadily due to shifting consumer preferences, market saturation, or superior new innovations. Companies eventually decide to harvest, pivot, reposition, or discontinue the product entirely.[[1]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CUtsYPGydKk)[[2]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0GsSTBI8Zkk&t=3)[[3]](https://www.surveymonkey.com/learn/market-research/5-stages-of-product-life-cycle/)[[4]](https://www.fool.com/terms/p/product-life-cycle/)


---

### Why the Product Life Cycle Matters
Understanding where a product sits in its life cycle helps business leaders make strategic decisions regarding:

- **Resource Allocation:** Deciding where to invest capital, staff time, and research and development.
- **Marketing and Pricing:** Shifting budgets from broad consumer awareness campaigns in early stages to retention, discounting, or product updates in later stages.
- **Extension Strategies:** Delaying decline by updating features, changing packaging, or finding new geographic markets.[[1]](https://www.surveymonkey.com/learn/market-research/5-stages-of-product-life-cycle/)[[2]](https://www.investopedia.com/terms/p/product-life-cycle.asp)[[3]](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/gZmIAUFQJ84)[[4]](https://fractory.com/product-life-cycle-explained/)
